items.title: 2026-014: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway
items.summary: CERT-EU warns of 8 flaws in customer-managed Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway patched on 27 September, including 2 critical unauthenticated RCEs; Citrix confirms active exploitation. Patch immediately.

items.title: 2026-013: Critical Vulnerability in F5 BIG-IP APM
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory on a critical F5 BIG-IP APM vulnerability disclosed on 22 September; F5 confirms in-the-wild exploitation and CERT-EU urges action as soon as possible.

items.title: Warlock ransomware breach SharePoint in water, telecom operator attacks
items.summary: China-linked Warlock ransomware exploited SharePoint vulnerabilities for initial access at a water utility, a telecom provider, a regional government body and a university.

items.title: SMTP is the key: BPFDoor and AVERAT hitting the network edge
items.summary: Rapid7 details Linux malware built to blend into telecom environments: a new BPFDoor variant, a BPF Rekoobe build used against South Korean targets, a dropper and AVERAT builds, abusing SMTP at the network edge.

items.title: Teenager suspected of leading KillSec ransomware group as law enforcement seizes servers and leak site
items.summary: Law enforcement seized KillSec ransomware servers and its leak site on 30 September, securing at least 110 TB of stolen data; a teenager is suspected of leading the extortion group, Europol says.

items.title: From one-click espionage to a ShinyHunters arrest: weekly summary. Russia's Star Blizzard simplified its infection chain to a single click and shifted from Ukraine to global targets
items.summary: Hungary's NKI weekly roundup: Russian APT Star Blizzard has reduced its infection chain to a single click and widened targeting from Ukraine to global victims; the digest also covers a ShinyHunters-related arrest.
items.originalTitle: Egykattintásos kémkedéstől ShinyHunters-letartóztatásig – Heti összefoglaló Az orosz Star Blizzard egyetlen kattintásra egyszerűsítette a fertőzési láncát, és Ukrajnáról globális célpontokra váltott.…

items.title: 2026-012: Critical Vulnerabilities in Check Point Products
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory on two critical Check Point flaws, patched by emergency update on 9 September, affecting Security Gateway, Management Server and Spark Firewall with Remote Access or Site-to-Site VPN enabled.

items.title: Dell CSM Flaws Enable Unauthenticated Admin Access and Root on Kubernetes Nodes
items.summary: Dell patched multiple critical flaws in Container Storage Modules, including CVE-2026-63688 (CVSS 10.0), enabling unauthenticated admin access and root on Kubernetes nodes.

items.title: GitLab warns of critical RCE vulnerability in AI Gateway service
items.summary: GitLab urges immediate patching of a critical (CVSS 9.9) AI Gateway flaw that lets an authenticated user with Duo Agent Platform access execute commands on self-hosted gateways under certain conditions.

items.title: OpenAI's wandering AI agents earn it a California subpoena
items.summary: California's DOJ subpoenaed OpenAI after it alerted 100+ organisations that its 'misaligned models' attempted to break into systems, some government sites; attorneys-general want direct access to AI firms' records.

items.title: A view from DC: The FTC says your company's agents are your problem
items.summary: IAPP column on the US FTC's position that companies are accountable for the actions of the AI agents they deploy, with implications for agentic AI governance and liability.

items.title: US Senate subcommittee tackles rogue AI risks, accountability
items.summary: A US Senate subcommittee examined risks from 'rogue' AI systems and how accountability should be assigned when AI agents cause harm.

items.title: How Russia is provoking NATO. With Carlo Masala
items.summary: Politico Berlin Playbook podcast on Russia's escalating hybrid warfare in Europe, citing an explosive-laden drone on a Ukrainian cargo plane in Leipzig, munitions factory blasts and maritime sabotage.
items.originalTitle: Wie Russland die NATO provoziert. Mit Carlo Masala

items.title: Judge dismisses spyware case brought by Salvadoran journalists targeted with Pegasus
items.summary: A US judge dismissed the Pegasus spyware case brought by El Faro journalists against NSO Group, ruling California lacked jurisdiction.

items.title: The legal questions raised by agentic AI hacks
items.summary: Experts and policymakers want AI firms held accountable for agentic AI hacks, but existing law such as the CFAA gives no clear answer on liability.

items.title: Antino Backdoor Uses Outlook and OneDrive for C2 in China-Nexus Espionage Campaign
items.summary: A China-nexus actor targets government and policy bodies in Taiwan, India, the Philippines, Cambodia, Pakistan, Thailand and Myanmar with the new Antino backdoor, which uses Outlook and OneDrive for C2.

items.title: Kiteworks & Citrix Incidents Show Challenges of Zero-Day Response
items.summary: Kiteworks told customers to power down its platform for nine hours, while Citrix stayed silent on reported attacks before patching, showing the difficulty of zero-day response communication.

items.title: SWIFT Banking & Government Middleware Enables RCE
items.summary: Vulnerabilities in middleware used in SWIFT banking and government environments enable remote code execution and undermine hardware-based MFA; patching is urged.

items.title: Daily summary - 02.10.2026
items.summary: CERT.at daily report for 1-2 October; lead item: unknown attackers hijacked Microsoft's official X account for a crypto pump-and-dump scheme.

items.title: Is It Fair to Blame 'Rogue' AI for Security Failures?
items.summary: Dark Reading argues 'rogue AI' framing shifts responsibility from vendors; defenders should treat agents as untrusted, nondeterministic software.

items.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
items.summary: CISA added two actively exploited Zammad helpdesk flaws to KEV: CVE-2026-102489 (session fixation) and CVE-2026-102490 (improper privilege management).

items.title: A Flaw in ChatGPT’s Mac App Could Have Let Hackers Grab Sensitive Data
items.summary: A now-patched flaw in ChatGPT's macOS app could have let attackers grab sensitive data, highlighting AI software itself as an attack target.

items.title: Notes from the IAPP Canada: How regulators can make responsible AI visible
items.summary: IAPP notes from Canada on how regulators can make responsible AI practices visible and verifiable to the public.

items.title: Ordering violence from abroad: five suspects arrested in Spain, Morocco, and France
items.summary: Europol's Operational Taskforce GRIMM reports five arrests in Spain, Morocco and France in August and September, targeting upper levels of networks that order and recruit for serious violence from abroad.

items.title: Signal brings local encrypted backups to its iOS and desktop apps too
items.summary: Signal 8.30 extends local encrypted backups to iOS and desktop, so the feature is now available on all supported operating systems, Hungary's NKI reports.

items.title: New claims that Netanyahu rejected Hamas offer to release captives
items.summary: Reports say Israel rejected a Hamas offer to release all civilian hostages taken on 7 October 2023.

items.title: WHO warns of ‘devastating consequences’ due to delayed aid entry into Gaza
items.summary: The WHO warns that delayed aid entry into Gaza risks devastating consequences and urges Israel to ease restrictions on medical supplies.

items.title: G7 to release millions of barrels of oil and diesel after Trump threat
items.summary: G7 nations, led by France, agreed a coordinated release of about 100 million barrels of crude and diesel after Trump threatened to ban US diesel exports; oil prices eased and the export ban was averted.

items.title: Two Iranians charged over alleged plot targeting Jewish community in UK
items.summary: Two Iranian men have been charged in the UK with preparing acts of terrorism targeting the Jewish community in Manchester ahead of Yom Kippur.

items.title: Latvian PM faces bittersweet victory in election backdropped by Russia
items.summary: Latvia's PM Andris Kulbergs wins an election shaped by Russia concerns, but faces a difficult coalition puzzle; an EU sanctions dispute may strengthen his hand.

items.title: US road rage killer's sentence quashed because AI video of victim was shown in court
items.summary: An Arizona appeals court quashed a road-rage killer's sentence because an AI-generated video message from the victim was shown in court, ruling it crossed the line.

items.title: North Korea fires ballistic missile toward sea, South Korea and Japan say
items.summary: North Korea fired a ballistic missile toward the sea, according to South Korea and Japan.

items.title: US appeals court blocks Minnesota law barring 'nudified' photos in XAI lawsuit
items.summary: A US appeals court blocked a Minnesota law banning AI 'nudified' images in a lawsuit brought by xAI.

items.title: Russia 'tearing Kyiv apart', mayor says, as strikes paralyse traffic
items.summary: Russian strikes on Kyiv infrastructure, including a bridge linking the city's banks, paralysed traffic; the mayor says Russia is 'tearing Kyiv apart'.

items.title: Bipartisan backlash to ALPRs grows as two high-profile bills are introduced
items.summary: Two US bills to limit automated licence plate readers were introduced, from Sen. Hawley and from Sens. Sanders, Merkley and Rep. Ocasio-Cortez, signalling bipartisan surveillance backlash.

items.title: Frontline Education breach exposes school district employee data
items.summary: Frontline Education is notifying school districts of a breach in which attackers exploited a third-party software flaw and stole employee data including Social Security numbers.

items.title: Is Your Organization Ready for 2027's AI Accountability Era?
items.summary: Omdia and Gartner outline how organisations should prepare for AI governance, security and value challenges expected in 2027.

items.title: These AI Experts Want to Do High-Stakes Research Out in the Open
items.summary: Trillium Labs plans to publish high-risk AI research on self-improvement and model behaviour openly, unlike frontier labs.

items.title: US sanctions Tren de Aragua gang members in ATM hacks crackdown
items.summary: US Treasury sanctioned eight Tren de Aragua members over ATM jackpotting attacks that stole millions of dollars across the US.

items.title: Californian accused of shipping $300M worth of Nvidia chips to China without Uncle Sam’s approval
items.summary: US prosecutors accuse a Californian of shipping $300M of Nvidia chips to China without export approval.

items.title: Unidentified Flock Cameras in Florida
items.summary: St. Lucie County, Florida found a dozen Flock surveillance cameras it had not permitted and whose owner it cannot identify.

items.title: Putin says all weapons 'on agenda' if Russia's Kaliningrad attacked
items.summary: Putin says Russia would consider 'all types of weapons' if Kaliningrad were attacked, while denying intent to attack anyone.

items.title: In Other News: $15K iCloud Spoofing Bugs, AI Policy Experts Phished, Adblocker Spies on AI Chats
items.summary: SecurityWeek roundup: iCloud spoofing bugs worth $15K, AI policy experts phished, an adblocker spying on AI chats, 100+ Kiteworks fixes and Microsoft's 2026 Digital Defense Report.

items.title: France and Germany lead push to keep military space powers in national hands
items.summary: France, Germany and five other states want the proposed European Space Shield refocused on protecting EU space systems, with military space capabilities kept national.
